members.text: Accelerating trunk rotation all the way through to the target instead of decelerating short of the target to release the shoulder
Trunk spins continuously without an anchor to decelerate, preventing momentum transfer to the arm and racket.
The player twists continuously through contact instead of allowing hip rotation to be transient and brake to create a whip effect.

groups.why_run1: Rotating the trunk continuously through contact instead of decelerating to transfer momentum to the arm.
groups.why_run2: Continuously rotating the trunk through contact rather than decelerating it to transfer momentum to the arm.

members.text: Pulling too close to the body or relying excessively on rotational body mechanics rather than pulling well out in front.
Catching the ball too late with the pull slot set too close to the stomach rather than out in front.

groups.why_run1: Pulling or setting the contact point too close to the body instead of extending well out in front.
groups.why_run2: Pulling or setting the racket pull slot too close to the body rather than out in front.

members.text: The player lets the hips drift forward and slides the knee forward over the toes instead of hinging at the hips and keeping the hips behind.
Hips extending forward in front of the shoulders with knees forward and chest up (quad dominant posture) rather than maintaining a hip hinge.

groups.why_run1: Pushing hips and knees forward instead of maintaining a hip hinge with hips back.
groups.why_run2: Allowing hips and knees to drift forward instead of maintaining a hip hinge.

members.text: Upper trapezius shrugging and lack of isometric engagement in the mid-traps and serratus anterior, detaching the hitting arm from the trunk.
Failure to stabilize the scapula with back and side muscles (lats, mid/lower traps) during forward drive.

groups.why_run1: Failing to stabilize the scapula with back muscles, detaching the hitting arm from the trunk.
groups.why_run2: Failing to stabilize the scapula with the mid-back musculature, disconnecting the hitting arm from trunk drive.
